scope: IDE-native shell review + fix: why the packaged Caret app did not behave like Cursor on a rebuilt bundle, and what now makes it work.
question: The user asked why Caret does not yet feel ide-native like Cursor, to read the latest handoff, and to continue the UI/UX shell with real functionality rather than mockups.

method.launch: packaged VSCode-darwin-arm64/Caret.app launched directly with a private --user-data-dir and a private caret.hostStateDir; no paid model calls
method.observation: No Chrome DevTools endpoint answered HTTP, and CUA timed out on the workbench accessibility tree, so the window was read three ways instead: (1) the extension's own LogOutputChannel written by the extension host, (2) the app's workspace/global storage databases, (3) a full-screen and per-window screencapture OCR'd locally with Apple Vision (swift).
method.vision: the vision model was rate limited for this session, so screenshots were read as OCR text runs with coordinates rather than as images

rootCause.symptom: On a freshly re-signed bundle the window opened, the agent dock was revealed, and the process stayed alive, but every persisted side effect silently stopped: no extension globalStorage directory, no mode-switch proof file, no workspace settings write.
rootCause.mechanism: Chromium stores its own 'Caret Safe Storage' item in the login keychain. The personal build is ad-hoc re-signed by every --package, which changes the code identity the keychain item's ACL is bound to. macOS therefore denies the read and raises a modal password prompt; while that prompt is up the main process is blocked and file/config writes never settle.
evidence: screen OCR: 'Caret wants to use your confidential information stored in "Caret Safe Storage" in your keychain. To allow this, enter the "login" keychain password.' with Always Allow / Deny / Allow
extension host log: caret.caret activated with activationEvent onStartupFinished and no error, yet globalStorage/caret.caret was never created
workspace storage: no Caret viewlet state was ever written
Caret output channel after the fix: 'startup view=ide mode=ide revealDock=true' plus a written mode-switch proof path
rootCause.control: Replaying the identical extension against a stubbed vscode module showed activate() completing and writing modeSwitchProof, so the failure was environmental, not in the startup logic.

observedShell.method: OCR text runs with pixel coordinates from a screencapture of the Caret window only (2880x1800)
shape: native menu bar: Caret / File / Edit / Selection / View / Go / Run / Terminal / Window / Help
left sidebar: EXPLORER, WORKSPACE, vscode, src, README.md  (native Explorer, not a webview substitute)
bottom: OUTLINE / TIMELINE panel with branch 'main*' and a left status bar item reading 'Caret ready'
right secondary sidebar titled CARET with view-title actions 'New Task' and 'Show IDE'

dock content: 'Ready' state dot, a context row 'Folder v Folder v This Mac v', a composer hint row 'Plan, Build, / for skills, @ for context', 'Model' and 'Thinking' controls, and idea rows (Start with a plan, Debug an issue, Build from a design, Deploy my prototype, Run in Cloud)
observedShell.conclusion: The agent surface is already a workbench citizen in the intended shape (dock beside native chrome, status bar item, view title actions, commands/keybindings/menus). The blocker was the Keychain stall, not missing shell work.

honestLimits: 'Run in Cloud' is an intentionally disabled affordance with reason 'Cloud is not a Caret runtime.'; it is not a working destination.

The dock reveal, status bar item, and menus are verified structurally (extension log, storage, manifest tests, pinned Code-OSS resolution tests) and by window OCR, not by pixel-level visual review, because the vision model was rate limited.
Mobile relay/iPhone gates are untouched by this slice.

apps/macos/src/extension.ts: the mode-switch proof write is now a fully catchable chain (Thenable wrapped) and reports a failed write instead of leaving an unhandled rejection

defectsFound.symptom: 'Add selection to task' (editor context menu, Cmd+Alt+K, and the composer's selection mention) demanded a selection but then cited the entire file, because the editor was only used when an explicit uri was passed.
defectsFound.found: by the new behavioral test asserting the citation for a two-line selection; it observed src/greet.ts#L1-L4 instead of #L1-L2
defectsFound.fix: the editor is now chosen from requireSelection (the selection/file distinction the call sites already make) plus a target match

defectsFound.symptom: caret.reviewInDiff reached from the command palette, a keybinding, or the Explorer opened a text diff of a binary file. The guard read binaryHint off the review snapshot, which only refreshReview populates; the direct command path never did, so the guard silently did nothing.
defectsFound.found: by the new behavioral test that modifies a committed .png and asserts no diff editor opens
defectsFound.fix: gitPathIsBinary(cwd, path) asks Git for the path's numstat and treats a '-' pair as binary; openNativeDiff consults it on every entry point

defectsFound.symptom: A failed mutating OMP request was indistinguishable from success. requestOmp swallowed every error and returned undefined, and the Thinking control and Fork task treated that as done, so picking a thinking level or forking could silently do nothing.
defectsFound.found: by auditing the remaining silent catch blocks after two earlier defects were hidden by the same pattern
defectsFound.fix: requestOmp logs the failure; ompCommandConfirmed() is the single 'did OMP confirm it' rule, and both mutation call sites report the honest reason
defectsFound.evidenceType: code audit plus unit tests of the rule and source assertions at both call sites; the end-to-end no-op needs a live host and was not reproduced in this harness

defectsFound.symptom: After 'Add selection to task' or 'Inline edit' the agent dock was never brought forward. focusDock executed `caretDock.focus`, but caretDock is the view *container*; Code-OSS registers a focus command per view as `<viewId>.focus` (viewsService.ts:562), so the id never existed, the rejection landed in a silent catch, and the user never saw where the cited text went.
defectsFound.found: by checking every command id the extension executes against the pinned Code-OSS source
defectsFound.fix: focusDock focuses caretComposerDock.focus with caretComposer.focus as fallback, and logs when neither view can be focused
defectsFound.test: apps/macos/test/ide-native-workbench.test.ts asserts the real view focus command is used and that the dead `caretDock.focus` id is gone; the test was confirmed to fail on the pre-fix code (it printed exactly ['caretDock.focus'])

agentEditMarks2026_09_14.scope: Give Caret's own edits a first-class place in the editor: mark the regions an applied edit produced, with one action to keep them and one to take them back. This is the Cursor-class affordance the objective's 'editor/selection actions' and 'native diff review' still lacked.

implemented.seam: CaretEditorService gained an optional afterApply(summary) report, fired only after a guarded apply passes its postcondition. It carries the path, uri, produced version, the pre-edit text, and the applied edits with their ranges. The apply decision itself is untouched, and a failure in the report cannot turn a successful apply into an error response.
implemented.geometry: apps/macos/src/agent-edit-marks.ts computes where each edit's replacement text landed in the new buffer (an edit never moves its own start, and the bridge rejects overlaps), merges touching or overlapping regions, widens a pure deletion to the whole line so it is visible, and counts the distinct lines for the label.
implemented.ui: A single decoration type paints the regions on every visible editor that has a pending Caret edit, with a hover naming the file and both actions. Commands caret.keepAgentEdit (saves the buffer, which is what 'kept' means for an unsaved change) and caret.revertAgentEdit (restores the exact pre-edit text) are offered from the editor title and the editor context menu, gated on the new caret.agentEditPending context key. A saved or closed document drops its pending record, so the buttons stay honest.
implemented.takeBackRule: revertDecision restores the pre-edit text only while the buffer still holds the version Caret produced. Once anything else has touched the buffer, the user's own work is in there too, so Caret declines with a reason and points at Undo instead of discarding it. Taking an edit back rewrites the buffer and never saves.

verified.notVerified: The painted mark has not been seen on a running editor from a real agent edit. Painting needs an applied edit, and the only thing that creates an editor request is OMP's `caret_editor` tool inside a live session with a chosen model: the host exposes no other driver (its CLI is serve/ensure/status, and the router has only the client-side register/poll/respond routes), and the fixture has no model chosen, so the send path itself honestly refuses there. The claim here is that the bridge reports the right change, the provider paints it, and the two commands act on it - each proven directly, with the commands additionally run in the real app - not that a screenshot of a painted mark exists.
